as_told.title: Christopher Dunn's work on the pyramid's engineering anomalies

plain: The idea is that the granite at the Giza pyramids in Egypt was cut with tools far more advanced than anything archaeologists have found there, an idea credited to a writer named Christopher Dunn, who studies what he calls engineering anomalies in the stonework. A former nuclear site guard named Mario Woods passes it on, saying the tools used to "carve or cut this granite are not in the archaeological array of tools of copper and wooden chisels today." Michels mentions Dunn more generally as someone who has "done all this work on just engineering anomalies with the thing itself," without speaking of tools or granite. If true, it would mean whoever built the pyramids had technology we cannot account for.
